title: prefill-decode-stage-overlap: chunked + speculative prefill scheduler and kernel selection improvements
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Prefill vs decode pipeline overlap has been a big source of variability in token throughput and tail latency for bursty workloads. Motivation: reduce end-to-end latency and increase sustained throughput for mixed prefill/decode workloads by improving chunked prefill scheduling, reducing kernel dispatch overhead, and making speculative prefill behavior less aggressive for long KV cache warmups. What this PR does: 1) Scheduler: introduce a lightweight stage-aware scheduler that prioritizes finishing short decode windows while allowing prefill chunking to proceed in parallel; uses a small credit system to bound prefill concurrency per GPU to avoid saturating the decode stage. 2) Chunked prefill: adaptive chunk sizing based on recent sequence-length distribution and measured kernel setup cost; small requests coalesce into micro-chunks, long requests are split into larger chunks to improve GPU kernel utilization. 3) Speculative prefill: add a conservative fallback path that disables speculative prefill when KV cache miss ratio is above a threshold or when observed prefill-decode overlap increases decode tail latency. 4) Kernel selection: add a runtime hint to choose the low-latency kernel path for decode-heavy slices and the throughput-oriented kernel for long prefill chunks. 5) Metrics and flags: new metrics pref/sched/credits, pref/chunk/size_histogram, pref/spec/disabled_reasons and runtime flags to tune thresholds. Performance: microbenchmarks on g4dn-like nodes show 8-12% throughput improvement for mixed workloads, 10-18% reduction in 99th percentile latency for decode-dominant traffic, and a 3-5% reduction in average tokens/GPU-hour on long prefill-heavy tests. Safety and rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag and experiment rollouts; default behavior unchanged until rollout hits 100%. Testing: unit tests for scheduler logic, integration tests with continuous-batching harness, replayed production traces (anonymized) for regression checks. CI: one flaky integration test initially failed on first run (race in scheduler test) and was fixed by adding deterministic scheduling in tests; full CI passed after fix. Related work: builds on prior prefill-decode overlap PRs pr-40621, pr-42342, pr-43021 and benchmarking in perf-canary. Linear: ENG-1987, ENG-2023. Checklist: - [x] design doc and benchmarks attached - [x] unit + integration tests added - [x] metrics and dashboards updated - [x] feature flag and rollout plan - [x] documentation note in runtime flags page Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/doc/ENG-1987 and benchmark dashboard (internal) Summary: modest but consistent perf wins with conservative defaults and feature flags to allow safe rollout.

review_comments: Ravi Singh: Can we avoid a global lock in scheduler.rs? The credit accounting looks like it might be contention on high concurrency. Reply (Maya): moved to per-GPU atomic counters and added a fast-path to avoid CAS churn.

Ava Thompson: The heuristic to disable speculative prefill based on KV miss ratio seems aggressive for cold starts. Suggest adding a cooldown window. Reply (Maya): added a 30s cooldown and a metric pref/spec/cooldown_events so we can track and tune.

Liam O'Connor: Please add a safety flag to force old behavior in case of regression in production. Reply (Maya): added runtime flag runtime.prefill.allow_stage_overlap and documented it in docs/runtime/flags.md.
CI Bot: integration test 'scheduler_determinism' failed on first run (race). Reply (Maya): fixed by introducing deterministic test harness and added explicit seeding for the test RNG.
release_notes: - Improved prefill-decode pipeline overlap with stage-aware scheduler and adaptive chunking. - Adds conservative speculative prefill fallback to avoid decode tail regressions. - Kernel path hints to reduce kernel dispatch overhead in mixed workloads.
